---
title: Other players and native apps
description: Play ClipMux videos in hls.js, Safari, ExoPlayer and any other HLS player, with the token in the URL path.
---

`<clipmux-player>` is the easy path in a web page, but nothing about ClipMux
needs it. A video is standard HLS: a master playlist, fMP4 (CMAF) segments,
a separate audio rendition and AES-128 encryption with the key served
beside the segments. Any player that plays that plays ClipMux. This page
covers the URL, how the token travels, and how to keep a long session
playing.

## Before you start

- A playback ID, and for a private video a token your backend signed; see
  [Sign playback tokens](/docs/build/play/sign-tokens).
- The media origin, `base_url`, from the video or from `GET /v1/app`. This
  page uses `https://media.example.com`.

## The URL

```txt
Private: https://media.example.com/v/{token}/{playback_id}/master.m3u8
Public:  https://media.example.com/p/{playback_id}/master.m3u8
```

The token is part of the path, not a query string or a header. Every
playlist, segment and key URL inside the master is relative, so the token
rides along to each of them without the player knowing. There are no
cookies and no custom headers to set, and delivery allows requests from any
origin (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`), so a web player on your own
domain needs no CORS setup.

What delivery answers, and what a player should do:

| Status | Meaning | Do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401 token_expired` | The token's `exp` has passed. | Get a new token and retry. |
| `403 denied` | The token is wrong for this video, or the app was disabled. | Stop. |
| `404` | The playback ID was revoked or doesn't exist, or the video isn't ready. | Stop, and show that the video is gone. |

## Keep long sessions playing

A token expires, and a player keeps fetching segments for as long as the
viewer watches. There are two ways to handle it:

1. **Renew the token.** A player that lets you change request URLs can swap
   a new token into the path when it sees a `401`. `@clipmux/player`
   exports helpers for this, shown for hls.js below.
2. **Sign for the whole session.** A player you can't hook into, including
   every native HLS player, gets a token that outlives the session. Sign it
   for the larger of twice the video's duration and 4 hours, within
   `max_token_lifetime_seconds` from `GET /v1/app` (7 days by default):

   ```ts
   const token = await clipmux.playback.token('pid_…', {
     native: true,
     durationSeconds: asset.duration_seconds, // 12 hours if you leave it out
   })
   ```

   In another language, set `exp` to `iat` plus that many seconds.

A longer token is a longer-lived URL: anyone who copies it can play the
video until it expires. Prefer renewal where the player allows it.

## hls.js

ClipMux's own tests play videos with plain hls.js. Load the master URL:

```ts
import Hls from 'hls.js'

const hls = new Hls()
hls.loadSource(`https://media.example.com/v/${token}/${playbackId}/master.m3u8`)
hls.attachMedia(video)
```

To renew tokens, wrap hls.js's loader with `createRefreshLoader` from
`@clipmux/player`. On a `401` it asks your callback for a new token once,
however many requests failed together, puts it into that request and every
later one, and retries. hls.js loads playlists, segments and keys through
the same loader, so this covers them all:

```ts title="player.ts"
import Hls from 'hls.js'
import { createRefreshLoader, type LoaderClass, playbackUrl, TokenSession } from '@clipmux/player'

const baseUrl = 'https://media.example.com'
const session = new TokenSession(firstToken, () => fetchTokenFromYourBackend(playbackId), {
  onDenied: () => video.pause(), // your callback returned null, or delivery said 403
})
const Base = Hls.DefaultConfig.loader as unknown as LoaderClass<{ url: string }>
const loader = createRefreshLoader(Base, session, baseUrl, playbackId)
const hls = new Hls({ loader: loader as unknown as typeof Hls.DefaultConfig.loader })
hls.loadSource(playbackUrl({ baseUrl, playbackId, token: session.current }))
hls.attachMedia(video)
```

Your callback returns a new token, or `null` to stop. A callback that throws
is retried after 1, 2 and 4 seconds. For a player with another loader or
request hook, `rewriteTokenUrl(url, mediaOrigin, playbackId, token)` puts a
token into a ClipMux URL and leaves any other URL alone.

## Safari and iOS

Safari plays HLS itself. ClipMux's tests play a private video in Safari with
a plain `<video>` element, including its separate audio track:

```html
<video src="https://media.example.com/v/eyJ…/pid_…/master.m3u8" controls playsinline></video>
```

Safari's own player can't renew a token mid-video, so sign for the whole
session. On iOS 17.1 and later, hls.js runs on Managed Media Source, so
hls.js with the refresh loader, or `<clipmux-player>`, can renew instead.

## Android with ExoPlayer

ClipMux's tests play a private video with Media3 ExoPlayer 1.5.1, including
its encryption and separate audio rendition. Add the HLS module:

```kotlin title="build.gradle.kts"
implementation("androidx.media3:media3-exoplayer:1.5.1")
implementation("androidx.media3:media3-exoplayer-hls:1.5.1")
```

and play the master URL:

```kotlin
val player = ExoPlayer.Builder(context).build()
player.setMediaItem(MediaItem.fromUri("https://media.example.com/v/$token/$playbackId/master.m3u8"))
player.prepare()
player.play()
```

Fetch the token from your own backend, which checks the viewer first, and
sign it for the whole session.

## Other players

Video.js, Shaka Player, AVPlayer on iOS and tvOS, and players on smart TVs
aren't covered by ClipMux's tests. They should play the same URL, since it
is standard HLS with AES-128, but check them yourself. Unless you can hook
the player's requests, sign tokens for the whole session.

AirPlay and Chromecast hand the URL to the receiving device, which fetches
the video itself, so nothing on the sending side can renew the token. Sign
those tokens for the whole session too. `<clipmux-player>` reports native
playback to your backend with `native: true`, but it can't tell whether the
viewer will cast, so a long session that starts in the browser and moves to
a TV may stop when its token expires.

## Subtitles and chapters

Ready subtitles are listed in the master playlist as an HLS subtitles
rendition, so players that show HLS subtitles find them with no extra
work. A player that wants a WebVTT file instead can fetch the sidecar URL:

```txt
https://media.example.com/v/{token}/{playback_id}/tracks/{track_id}.vtt
```

Chapters are never in the master playlist. Fetch the chapters track's VTT
from the same URL form, and `parseChapters` from `@clipmux/player` reads it
into `{ startTime, endTime, title }` in seconds. See
[Chapters](/docs/build/captions/chapters).

## Check it works

```bash
curl -s "https://media.example.com/v/$TOKEN/pid_…/master.m3u8" | head
```

A `200` with `#EXTM3U` and `#EXT-X-STREAM-INF` lines means the URL is right.
If the player still fails, open its network log: a `401` partway through a
session means the token expired and nothing renewed it.
